channel.description: An aggregated feed of Technology-related news

item.title: The disadvantages of owning smart refrigerators
item.description: A smart refrigerator can change how you manage your kitchen, but its features come with practical drawbacks worth checking before making a purchase.

item.title: After the midterms, things are looking rocky for Elon Musk and data centers
item.description: On Equity, we unpacked what the midterms mean for the tech industry.

item.title: Hitman World of Assassination devs say Elusive Targets are captured from studying talent over many hours and 'bespoke craftsmanship' rather than scans — 'You can have the 3d mesh completely right and still not feel like it looks like the person'
item.description: IO Interactive has revealed that it hand-crafts all of its Hitman World of Assassination Elusive Targets rather than relying on traditional scanning.

item.title: Is your router overheating? Here's how to keep it cool and working safely
item.description: You'll want your router to be well-ventilated for it to perform at its best.

item.title: How often should you restart your Fitbit watch?
item.description: The old "turn it off and turn it on again" trick can come in handy for certain situations.

item.title: The built-in iPhone app for creativity you may be ignoring (but shouldn't)
item.description: Your iPhone has a built-in app for brainstorming and visual planning that can turn scattered screenshots, sketches and notes into something you can share.

item.title: Megaspeed exec was recruited to spy on Nvidia CEO, according to US intelligence memo
item.description: A memo circulated earlier this year reportedly claimed that China’s Ministry of State Security recruited a female technology executive to spy on Nvidia's CEO.

item.title: Your EV's battery is big enough to run your house — here's what stops most people
item.description: Today's EV batteries could let you power specific appliances or your entire house. But a few factors line up to make that idea a non-starter for most folks.

item.title: Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 14 Aura laptop gets $500 off for Black Friday
item.description: Lenovo's premium ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 14 Aura Edition laptop gets a $500 discount for Black Friday

item.title: Your old iPod could be a sleeper flash drive
item.description: Old iPods still work fine as digital audio players, but you can reuse them in other ways if you're not interested in listening to music on the go.

item.title: There is no end in sight for the GPU supply problem
item.description: GPU prices have soared as the supply of memory has tightened, and it doesn't look like this is going to change any time soon (though a few optimists disagree).
